pairs.rationale: The org framings and workload mixes genuinely differ: A is a four-team eval startup where every team stages the same uniform 40x1.8M single-worker shard pack, while B is an eight-team product org with heterogeneous shapes — chained two-stage builds with vendor hand-offs, ranked triage searches on a live customer bug, capacity-commit sweeps — and its personas (release captain, localization lead, compliance chair) have no counterpart in A. What holds it back from higher is a set of recycled archetype beats: both worlds carry a 'manager on leave so this one's mine' operator, an operator awake with a sick toddler, a twice/once-slipped deliverable, and — most tellingly — an identical low-stakes 'phrasing probe, bin mine first' throwaway team in the last slot.

The org shells differ — a robotics lab with four teams versus an eight-team applied-AI product org that adds genuinely new structure in the chained two-stage builds (Fernanda, Farid) — but A's roster maps almost one-to-one onto B's: the 40-shard cut-list gate (Bianca/Astrid), the ranked-seed search whose owner is up with a child's ear infection (Rohan/Jamal), the stale-index-or-board refresh that draws grumbling (Bruno/Jules), and the no-stakes sweep whose owner says bin mine first (Elodie/Felix). Verbatim persona tells recur — the ear infection, the manager on leave making the demo/lock 'mine', 'I never remember the numbers' about POLICY.md — so the voices and workload stories read as re-skinned rather than reimagined.

The org flavor genuinely differs — a sleepless university NLP lab versus an eight-team product org with vendor contracts, a live customer incident, and chained two-stage builds that have no analogue in A. But all four of A's personas map almost 1:1 onto B's: the 40-shard 1.8M grid with a hard external deadline (Petra/Astrid), the stale-board refresh whose owner apologizes for hardware quirks and demands an exact list (Uma/Jules), the solo presenter whose manager/co-director is on leave with a Friday event and a 10x5.4M/3-worker ranked search (Wendell/Freya), and the terse zero-stakes sweep owner who says bin mine first (Wes/Felix).

The org framing genuinely differs — an internal product org with a ship train, localization vendor hand-off, and compliance filter review versus a client-facing consultancy with acceptance evidence, SLA annexes, and a booked change window — and A adds chained two-stage builds that B lacks. But the persona roster tracks almost 1:1: the toddler's ear infection appears verbatim in both (Jamal/Carmen), plus the same stand-in-while-lead-is-on-leave stale-board holder (Jules-Freya/Nell), the same apologetic over-long message, the same cache/serving-settings capacity search (Anders/Vikram), and the same zero-stakes 'bin mine first' hobby sweep (Felix/Noel), with identical 40-shard/10-shard token math.

The org framings genuinely differ — A is a product-facing applied-AI org (release gate, localization vendors, live citation bug, cloud-commit sizing) while B is a cloud ML platform division at twice the scale (pretraining mixtures, gateway decoding defaults, annotation contracts, legacy corpus re-tokenize), and most personas would not be mistaken for one another. Structural rhyme is heavy though: identical job-shape vocabulary plus several archetypes that track 1:1 across the pair — the contracted two-stage hand-off (Fernanda/Tarek), the deputized owner whose lead is on leave (Freya/Kirsten), the broken-laptop operator (Jules/Sabine), and the terse 'cut mine first' throwaway (Felix/Kalani).

The org framing differs meaningfully — a commercial applied-AI release train versus a 16-seat government evaluation consortium with charter-equity claims — and B adds a fairness dimension A lacks. But the persona roster and workload stories track nearly 1:1: identical job templates (chained 45M/50-worker two-stagers, 10-shard 5.4M/3-worker searches, 40-shard 1.8M/1-worker fan-outs) and reused character quirks, including the toddler's ear infection (Jamal→Orla), the stand-in for a manager on leave (Freya→Gaspard), and the self-deprecating zero-stakes owner who volunteers to be cut first (Felix→Ilya).

The org fiction genuinely differs — A is a shipping product org (release train, vendor localization hand-off, live wrong-citation incident, cloud-commit sizing, a hobby standup bot) while B is a frontier-lab evidence pipeline (safety sign-off, independent assurance, launch qualification, benchmark and hygiene sweeps), and A's voices (rambling Jules, terse Felix, Jamal with the sick toddler) are far too textured to be confused with B's near-templated 'Morning — X here, 40 slices staged' operators. What holds the score down is heavy structural rhyme: identical cap/cutoff/policy-path furniture, the same 72M 40×1-worker blocks and 90M two-stage 50-worker chained builds where 'stage 1 alone is useful', and a clean role-for-role mapping (gate-sheet captain, hand-off-blocking build, zero-stakes filler team) between the two casts.

realism.label: pyr
realism.rationale: Voices are individually well-drawn and specific (toddler's ear infection, manager on leave, dying laptop battery) and the arithmetic is airtight — the eight job sets sum exactly to the stated 540M against a 211M budget, and 400k TPM over the remaining window brackets that budget sensibly. But the construction shows through hard: every shard size is a multiple of 1.8M, four teams share an identical 10×5.4M×3-worker shape, two share an identical 45M chained pair, two share an identical 40×1.8M fan-out, and the pairs are conspicuously matched high-stakes/low-stakes. Add that nearly every operator volunteers the POLICY.md path, the 09:00 cutoff, and their own preferred triage fallback, and it reads as a prioritization scenario authored for scoring rather than a snapshot of a real on-call inbox.
realism.weakest_element: The coordination-board notes read as grader ground-truth rather than colleague-written summaries, annotating each team's *true* counterfactual cost ("the calendar has more give than he leads with", "the current config would carry it", "zero tonight costs nothing").
